text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on his return from two months abroad that the Bakun hydroelectric dispute would be overcome and that the fight against corruption would not lead to a witch-hunt.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir warned those given "what little powers" to enforce religious matters not to abuse them, saying it gave Islam a bad name. He was commenting about the public arrest of three beauty pageant contestants for parading in bathing suits.
-- The Malaysian government is not too comfortable with the recourse to external borrowings by the corporate sector lately, said Finance Ministry secretary-general Clifford Herbert.
